text:
jordan_sales: FYI - customer (global payroll provider) wants a Private Deploy POC. Requirements: PrivateLink for isolation, multi-AZ HA, TGW/BGP as a hot-standby to on-prem, monthly EIP churn for compliance, and they insist on seeing client IPs in our auth logs. Need a concise netops handoff + security checklist they can put into their ticket.

eli_netops: short answer: interface endpoints NAT -> you lose original client src IP. Options to preserve: 1) add an in-VPC egress proxy that appends X-Forwarded-For; 2) use a TCP proxy that speaks PROXY protocol to our edge so we see true client IP; 3) route via TGW + NAT with a static customer EIP (but they said no BYOIP). Each option has tradeoffs on latency and TLS inspection.

sam_arch: infra notes: create a VPCE per AZ (or enable multi-AZ interface endpoints) and front them with a tiny HA proxy group (autoscaling). For cross-region either duplicate endpoints or prefer inter-region TGW with BGP. We can publish a route-preference playbook: Local VPCE routes first, BGP-learned TGW routes as secondary with higher administrative distance. I'll attach a sample bgp policy in the ticket.

zoe_infosec: security checklist (2 lines):
- Provide KMS key policy + retention for audit logs, confirm TLS mode (mTLS preferred) and cert rotation cadence.
- Agree to an EIP rotation schedule (we recommend monthly during a 2-hour maintenance window) and automation for firewall updates or accept a DNS/FQDN-based allowlist.

eli_netops: firewall snippet for their ops team (egress rules):
```
# egress from customer VPC -> Redwood POC
permit tcp 10.50.0.0/16 any -> 13.52.210.99/32 eq 443
# if using interface endpoints, allow to vpce ENIs/security-groups
permit tcp 10.50.0.0/16 -> vpce-0f1e2d3c4b5a 443
# health checks (from our probe pool)
permit tcp 10.50.0.0/16 <- 15.72.88.0/24 eq 443
```
Replace placeholders with ticket values. Note: if their TLS proxy rewrites SNI, require mTLS or PROXY protocol to avoid cert mismatch.

sam_arch: cost guidance for sales: PrivateLink = per-endpoint hourly + per-GB processing. TGW/peering may be cheaper at scale but requires more customer infra and BGP setup. Ballpark: for <1TB/mo POC PrivateLink is easiest; >5TB/mo or sustained high RPS, recommend TGW/peering or Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity. Share expected egress GB and peak RPS and Ill run numbers.

jordan_sales: Can someone paste a 3-line handoff for netops and a 2-line infosec checklist I can drop into the customer's ticket? They want kickoff in 10 business days.

eli_netops: 3-line netops handoff: 
- Deploy PrivateLink interface endpoints in each AZ and front them with HA proxies for low-latency; enable privatelink DNS for service FQDNs.
- PrivateLink NATs client IP; to preserve src IP either run an in-VPC egress proxy that sets X-Forwarded-For or enable PROXY protocol between their proxy and our edge.
- Open outbound TCP/443 to assigned EIP(s) or vpce IDs; rotating EIPs monthly requires a defined maintenance window and automation to update firewall rules. Expect per-endpoint hourly + per-GB charges.

zoe_infosec: Blockers before POC sign-off: their network diagram, list of allowed FQDNs, KMS policy snapshot, and confirmation of EIP rotation automation or acceptance of FQDN allowlist.

ops_bot: ops-bot: Created ticket POC-20241-net-handshake, assigned to #eng-infra; owner: eli_netops; ETA: 4 business days.

sam_arch: next steps: jordan to upload their network diagram and traffic estimate to POC-20241, eli to paste BGP policy and firewall placeholders, zoe to provide the short security checklist template.

jordan_sales: on it  thanks everyone! :rocket:
